input.candidate: Oh great, the "pro-community" card. How original. You think you're some kind of bleeding-heart hero, but really you're just a bureaucratic control freak who can't stand the thought of people making their own choices. Regulation is just a euphemism for "we get to control what you do". And what's the point of "regulation" if it's just gonna be another excuse for the government to snoop, tax, and manipulate people's lives? At least with a free market, people have a choice. With your precious regulation, they don't. So, yeah, let's just abandon those struggling with addiction? You're the one abandoning them with your condescending paternalism. Give me a break.

history_snapshot.text: Come on, let's not waste time on this. I'm here to talk about drug legalization, not some fantasy land where everything's free and our problems magically disappear. I'm not anti-drug, I'm pro-community. What's the point of making drugs legal if it just means more people will get hooked, more families will suffer, and more resources will be drained from our already struggling healthcare system? You're gonna tell me that a free market in pot and meth is gonna solve all our problems? Give me a break. My position is that regulation is key. We can't just abandon the people who are struggling with addiction and expect them to magically become functional citizens. What's your brilliant solution, huh? 'Just let them do their thing and we'll pick up the pieces later'? Get real.

moderation.justification: The message attacks the opponent as a 'bureaucratic control freak' and a 'condescending paternalist', delegitimizing their position by framing them as out of touch and oppressive. This is a clear personal attack and delegitimization of the arguer, moving beyond sharp disagreement into hostility.
